what: Venture Global builds and operates liquefied natural gas export terminals on the US Gulf Coast. It uses modular, factory-built liquefaction units rather than custom-built trains, which it says lets it build faster and cheaper than rivals.
customers: European and Asian utilities and energy companies under long-term contracts, plus spot cargo buyers.
money: long-term contracted cargoes and commissioning volumes sold at spot prices
moat: A modular construction approach that has brought plants online years faster than conventional LNG projects, in a market where speed to first cargo is worth billions.
risks: Debt of about $46 billion funds construction, an enormous figure relative to earnings
Customers have brought arbitration claims over cargoes sold at spot prices during commissioning instead of delivered under contract
Spot gas prices determine the value of uncontracted volumes
Construction of further plants carries execution risk
opportunities: Revenue grew about 177% last year as new capacity came online
Analysts see about 45% upside from current levels
Long-term contracts provide fixed fees once plants move out of commissioning
watch: Construction milestones, the arbitration outcomes, and the share of volumes under long-term contract.
